title: The digest page, four dollars
logline: The 2001 laundromat page, matted at full price, in a thrift-store bin: $4. The dog under the table, behind glass, priced. He doesn't buy it. He draws it in the bin.

panels.composition: A thrift store's bin of frames: among them, face up, a small framed quarter-letter zine page — a four-panel strip with a dog under a table — the mat yellowed, a $4 tag on the glass. The reflection of a window's light across the top panel.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a thrift-store bin of secondhand frames with a small framed yellowed zine page showing a four-panel comic with a dog under a table lying face up among them, a four-dollar tag on the glass, window light across it, no words
image.notes: dw_2001-03-07's frame, twenty-three years on. Letter after: $4. He leaves it.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: 'Frame's the same.' Four dollars. Left in the bin.
